Fit a reduced-rank generalised dissimilarity model

Source: R/fit_rrGDM.R
rrGDM.Rd

Fit a reduced-rank Generalised Dissimilarity Model using TMB

Usage

rrGDM(
  Y,
  X = NULL,
  k = 2,
  binary = FALSE,
  formula = ~.,
  formula_sd = ~1,
  dist_method = "bray",
  scale_diss = NULL,
  family = "gaussian",
  link = NULL,
  se = TRUE,
  sample_error = TRUE,
  constraint = 1,
  trans = function(x) x,
  sparse = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  init_jitter = 0.1,
  n_starts = 1,
  previous_best = TRUE,
  init_method = "dbRDA",
  start_fit = NULL,
  trace = FALSE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

Y

A matrix or data frame containing the response variable (usually species abundance matrix).

X

A data frame containing the predictor variables.

k

An integer specifying the number of latent variables to be used in the model. Default is 2.

binary

Logical indicating whether the response variable should be treated as binary (e.g., presence-absence). Default is FALSE.

formula

Formula specifying the model to be fitted.

formula_sd

Formula specifying the model for the dispersion parameter. Default is ~1 (intercept only).

dist_method

A character string specifying the distance method to be used (e.g., "euclidean", "bray"). Default is "bray".

scale_diss

A numeric vector of length two indicating a new scale for dissimilarities. Useful for distributions bounded between 0 and 1 (e.g., beta family). Ignored, with a warning, for the "binomial" and "beta.binomial" families.

family

A character string specifying the family of the response variable: "gaussian", "binomial", "beta" or "beta.binomial". Default is "gaussian".

link

Character string specifying the link function to be used: "identity", "negexp" or "neggaus". Default is 'identity' for Gaussian distribution, and 'negexp' for beta and binomial distributions.

se

Logical indicating whether to calculate standard errors (TRUE) or not (FALSE). Default is TRUE.

sample_error

Logical. If TRUE, includes site-level random effects to account for variation not explained by predictors. Default is TRUE.

constraint

Integer. Specifies identifiability constraints. 0: no constraint; 1: Constraint applied to environmental loadings matrix (\(\Lambda\)); 2: Constraint applied to site random effects matrix (U). Default is 1.

trans

Function used to transform the response matrix before computing dissimilarities (e.g., log, sqrt). Default is no transformation.

sparse

Optional object of class sparse_diss (see sparse_diss). If supplied, the model is fitted using only the pairs of samples listed in sparse$edges, instead of all pairs. It must be created from the same samples as Y. Default is NULL (all pairs).

seed

An integer passed to set.seed() at the start of the fit, so it changes the state of R's random number generator. Default is NULL (no seed is set).

init_jitter

Numeric. Standard deviation of the Gaussian noise added to the starting values of every start after the first. Only used when n_starts > 1. Default is 0.1.

n_starts

Integer. Number of optimisation starts. The first start uses the values from init_method (or start_fit); each further start adds Gaussian noise (SD init_jitter) to the best solution so far (previous_best = TRUE) or to the initial values (FALSE). With more than one start, only fits that converged and have a positive-definite Hessian are eligible as the final fit. Default is 1.

previous_best

Logical. Controls where the jitter for multiple starts after the first is applied. If TRUE (default), each start jitters around the best solution found so far (perturb-and-reoptimise). If FALSE, every start jitters around the initial values (from init_method), so starts do not depend on earlier fits. Only relevant when n_starts > 1.

init_method

A character string specifying a method used to obtain initial values for optimisation. Currently, only 'PCOA' and 'dbRDA' are available; NULL starts from small random values. Default is 'dbRDA'. Ignored if start_fit is supplied.

start_fit

Optional fitted rrGDM model used to initialise the optimisation (e.g., a fast sparse fit before refitting with more pairs). It must have the same samples, k, family, link, constraint, predictors and random-effect structure as the new model; the set of pairs (sparse) may differ. If supplied, init_method is ignored. Default is NULL.

trace

Logical. If TRUE, TMB prints the optimisation progress and the objective of each start is reported. Default is FALSE.

control

A list of control parameters passed to nlminb. iter.max defaults to 1000.

Value

An object of class "rrGDM": a list with the components below.

Estimation

opt

Result of nlminb for the fixed-effect parameters

obj

The TMB object created by MakeADFun

best_par

Numeric vector with estimated parameters at the optimum, including the modes of random effects

sd_rep

An sdreport object with standard errors and the covariance matrix of the estimates, or NULL if se = FALSE or the standard errors could not be computed. See include_se

pd_hess

TRUE if the Hessian at the optimum is positive definite and not nearly singular, FALSE if not, and NA if there is no sd_rep

Data

Y, X

The community matrix and the predictor data as supplied

Y_diss, Y_den

Observed values for the fitted pairs. For the "gaussian" and "beta" families, Y_diss is the dissimilarity (rescaled to scale_diss if given) and Y_den is 1. For "binomial" and "beta.binomial", Y_diss is the numerator of the dissimilarity and Y_den the denominator, so that Y_diss / Y_den is the dissimilarity.

pairs

Two-column matrix with the row numbers of Y of the two samples in each fitted pair, in the same order as Y_diss.

sparse

The sparse_diss object supplied in sparse, or NULL if all pairs were used.

obs_full

Only for fits with sparse: observed dissimilarities of all pairs of samples, in the order of dist

Design matrices

X_design

Design matrix of the predictors in formula (samples x predictors, without intercept; zero columns if there are no predictors).

W_design

Design matrix of formula_sd (samples x terms, with intercept)

Z_design

Sparse indicator matrix for the random intercepts in formula (samples x total number of groups).

map_re

Integer vector giving, for each column of Z_design, the random-effect term it belongs to (index into re_vars). integer(0) if there are no random effects.

re_vars

Names of the grouping variables with random intercepts. character(0) if there are none.

Model specification

k, family, link

Number of latent dimensions, family and link used

inv_link

Function that maps distances in the latent space to expected dissimilarities (identity, \(1 - e^{-d}\) or \(1 - e^{-d^2}\)).

constraint

Identifiability constraint used

formula, formula_sd

The formulas supplied.

formula_fix

formula without the random-effect terms (~0 if there are no predictors).

terms_fix, terms_sd

terms objects of the fixed-effect and formula_sd models.

xlevels_fix, xlevels_sd, contrasts_fix, contrasts_sd

Factor levels and contrasts used to build the design matrices. Used to build the design matrices for new data.

call

The matched call.

Details

With constraint = 1 (or 2) the upper triangle of the loadings \(\Lambda\) (or of the sample-level errors \(U\)) is fixed at 0 so that the model is identifiable. A positive diagonal is currently not imposed, so the sign of a latent axis is arbitrary.

See also

summary.rrGDM, anova.rrGDM, wald_test, get_LV, predict.rrGDM, biplot.rrGDM, stress, cor_r2, include_se, sparse_diss

Examples

  # Toy community with 25 sites, 25 species, 2 environmental gradients
  set.seed(2)
  n <- 25 # sites
  p <- 25 # species

  env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n))
  eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)
  Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p)

  fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,
               formula = ~ temp + moist,
               family = "binomial")
#> ℹ Preparing data
#> ✔ Preparing data ... done
#> 
#> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA)
#> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done

#> ℹ optimisation

#> ✔ optimisation ... done
#> 
  summary(fit)
#> Call:
#> rrGDM(Y = Y, X = env, k = 2, formula = ~temp + moist, family = "binomial")
#> 
#> Family: binomial (link: negexp); 2 latent dimensions; 25 samples (300 pairs)
#> Log-likelihood: -1670.17 (df = 4); AIC: 3348.33

#> ── Effects on composition (location) ──
#> 
#>   term   Size    Wald Df Pr_Chisq Sig
#>   temp 0.5957 603.881  1   <1e-06 ***
#>  moist 0.6527 644.000  2   <1e-06 ***
#> ── Effects on dispersion (log of sample-level SD) ──
#> 
#>         term Estimate     SE      z   Pr_z Sig
#>  (Intercept)   -2.030 0.1088 -18.66 <1e-06 ***
#> 
#> Sample-level SD at baseline: tau = exp(Intercept) = 0.1313
#> ── Fit of the latent space (conditional) ──

#>   Stress (metric, response scale):    0.06025
#>   Stress (non-metric, link scale):    0.09938
#>   corR2:                              0.9550

#>   not the explanatory power of the predictors.

#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

  # Model the sample-level dispersion too
  fit2 <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,
                formula = ~ temp + moist,
                formula_sd = ~ temp,
                family = "binomial")
